gate: Watch what happens when a person carrying this code walks into a room. There is a pull toward closeness that does not wait to be invited. The code is sexuality at its widest sense, not only the bedroom meaning but the whole drive to break through what keeps two people separate. It is reproductive in the deep sense, the force that makes new bonds, new families, new groupings out of what was apart. Most people read this drive as too much. The intensity gets named pushy, or invasive, or hungry. That misread costs the code its real work. The work is not seduction. It is the ability to find the seam in another person's guard and to bring warmth across it. A person with this gate does not always know they are doing it. The pressure is just there, low in the body, asking to connect.
centre_field: Low in the belly sits the body's powerhouse, the part of the chart that runs on life force and response. It is the motor for work and for sex, and the two are not separate down here. Both are the same energy aimed at different rooms. That placement is the whole teaching. Sexuality at this code is not a story told in the head. It is a yes or a no rising up from the gut before the mind catches up. The centre does not negotiate. It opens, or it closes. To live this gate through the head is to feel the pull and the closure as two contradictory commands. They are one signal, read from the wrong floor. The centre asks for the body to be trusted as the first reader. Heat rises, or it does not. The information is already there.
channel: A code like this is built incomplete on purpose. It reaches across to the gate of friction, and the two together form the channel of mating. The reach is what makes the work real. The drive to break through closeness, on its own, is undirected heat. It can spill toward anyone, scatter itself, mistake any warm body for the right one. The friction gate is what gives it edges, an emotional weather that sorts which bond is actually wanted and which is just the pressure looking for somewhere to land. Joined, the code becomes the slow work of making families, partnerships, true intimacies. Alone, it is intensity without a target. The partner side is what teaches this drive to wait, to feel, to know which closeness is the real one. The code is not finished until it meets that other half.
